summary: Mechanism plausible, but most of the predicted decode_32 gain is already explained by the smaller grid: unpaired S=8 at B=32 (sliding-decode32-splits-8) reached 17.3 us, inside this hypothesis's 16-19 us target. Run it with an unpaired same-grid control, and only after sliding-cluster-s2-decode-c4-pdl-inproc reports: that check serves exactly these shapes, and if it meets its gate this Triton path stops running on any scored shape.
justification: _sliding_fused_kernel takes 12.9 us at decode_16 (floor 1.65) and 22.1 us at decode_32 (floor 3.29): latency/per-program-overhead bound. Pairing saves one page-table load per token, the 8 padding rows of M=16 (MMA, exp2, fp32 partials; half of 4 MB workspace at B=32), one new-key build and one combine per request, and halves the programs. Weakest link: 'half the gather instructions' is false in Triton (16 B per thread per load; same instruction count and DRAM sectors grid-wide), so the FA3 head-pairing precedent (issue-bound 80K gathers) does not carry over. Halving programs partly undoes deep-splits (which gained decode_16 by 128->512 programs), so decode_16 'faster' is the least supported prediction. Sliding is ~21-23% of the decode_16/32 loads; a 2-5 us kernel gain moves the headline ~0.5-0.8%, inside CI. Judge on _sliding_fused_kernel time per shape.
confounders: sliding-deep-splits-on-cuda-splitkv (landed): pairing halves the grid, so program count and pairing are confounded at both shapes.
sliding-fused-triton-decode1-gate (landed): counter key changes (B,2)->(B,1) and the combine becomes per-b; recheck the zero-reset invariant.
fa3-hdim128-head-pairing / paired-heads-launch-cleanup: full layers only; their gain is not evidence for this regime.
full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv: does not touch sliding shapes.
interference: One companion: an unpaired S=8 same-grid control (B x 2 x 8 programs, 16 KB each) so paired minus control isolates pairing. Interaction: sliding-cluster-s2-decode-c4-pdl-inproc (running) gates all sliding decode 1<=B<=32 onto a CUDA cluster kernel with better targets (decode_16 <=10, decode_32 <=12 us); mutually exclusive, not stackable. WAIT for that result before dispatching this pair. If it lands, drop both; if it fails, ties, or lands only at one batch, run this pair.
rules_flags: No rule problems: config-only predicate, bf16 operands, every key scored, no host sync, counters hold no input data.
Correctness hazard: the new-key build over the 128-wide k slice must apply RMSNorm per 64-wide head half and RoPE freq must index (d % 64)//2.
Each row's output must come from its own kv-head half of acc[16,128] in both the partial write and the epilogue; discard the other half.

companions.change: From master (the parent's base), change only the split count in _sliding_forward: splits = 8 if (length == 1 and batch > 1 and hkv == 2) else (16 if length == 1 else _num_splits(batch, hkv)). Keep _sliding_fused_kernel, the unpaired gather (program (b, g, s), 64-byte rows), M=16 with its padding rows, BLOCK_N 64, num_warps 4, num_stages 2, the ticket counters _counters(batch, hkv), and the workspace sizing. Batch 1 decode stays at S=16; verify and full layers unchanged byte for byte. Grid (B, 2, 8): 256 programs at B=16, 512 at B=32, each 256 keys x 64 B = 16 KB: the same grid and bytes per program as the paired hypothesis, without the pairing.
companions.reason: Separates pairing from the grid halving that pairing also brings; pairing's effect = paired minus control kernel time per shape.
